title: UBQ Materials

{{Short description|Israeli cleantech company}} {{Infobox company | name = UBQ Materials | logo = UBQ Logo 72 dpi RGB.png | logo_caption = UBQ Materials Logo | type = Privately held company | industry = Materials | founded = July 2012 | key_people = Albert Douer, Chairman and CEO
[[Jack (Tato) Bigio]], Co-Founder & Chief Growth and Sustainability Officer | products = Thermoplastic composite made from mixed household wastemade | hq_location_city = [[Tel Aviv]] | hq_location_country = Israel | website = {{URL|ubqmaterials.com}} }} '''UBQ Materials''' is a global manufacturing company created to convert mixed household waste including all organic content into a [[thermoplastic]] composite. The company's primary product, UBQ, is a bio-based thermoplastic sold in the form of tablets or masterbatch that can replace or enhance conventional plastics in the manufacturing of durable or semi-durable products.{{Cite news|last1=Morrison|first1=Jim|last2=Kordova|first2=Shoshana|date=2019-11-18|title=Revolutionary recycling? A new technology turns everyday trash into plastic treasure.|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/graphics/2019/climate-solutions/israeli-startup-ubq-turning-trash-into-plastic-products/|access-date=|newspaper=Washington Post}}{{Cite web|last=Zion|first=Ilan Ben|title=Waste recycling: Israeli business says it can turn garbage into plastic products|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/energy/2018/03/22/israeli-firm-can-turn-garbage-into-plastic-gold/448638002/|access-date=2020-08-20|website=USA TODAY|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|last1=Tomlinson |first1=By Chris |date=2020-05-04|title=Tomlinson: Israeli company challenges plastic industry with material made from garbage|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/business/columnists/tomlinson/article/Israeli-company-challenges-Texas-plastic-industry-15238626.php|access-date=2020-08-20|website=HoustonChronicle.com|language=en-US}} UBQ is used in several applications across many industries, specifically in building & [[construction]], [[Durable good|consumer durables]], supply chain & logistics, [[Automotive industry|automotive]], and [[retail]]. In 2018, UBQ Materials Ltd. became a Certified [[B Corporation (certification)|B Corporation]].{{Cite web|url=https://bcorporation.net/directory/ubq-materials-ltd|title=U.B.Q MATERIALS LTD | Certified B Corporation|website=bcorporation.net}} In 2023, [[Time (magazine)|Time magazine]] listed UBQ technology as life-changing.[https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-11-17/ty-article-magazine/.highlight/life-changing-israeli-startup-picks-up-the-pieces-after-october-7-tragedy/0000018b-decf-df9a-ab8b-decfedce0000 Life-changing Israeli start-up picks up the pieces after October 7 tragedy] ==History== UBQ Materials was founded in 2012 by Yehuda Pearl (co-founder of [[Sabra (company)|Sabra]]), Jack (Tato) Bigio, and Eran Lev.{{Cite web |last=Shemer |first=Simona |date=2020-11-02 |title=Israel's UBQ Partners With Mainetti To Boost Sustainability In Fashion |url=https://nocamels.com/2020/11/mainetti-ubq-materials-sustainability-fashion/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=NoCamels |language=en-US}} The company developed and patented a process to convert mixed [[municipal solid waste]], including organics, into a [[thermoplastic]] material known as UBQ. The proprietary and patented product and manufacturing method were developed, tested, and validated between 2012 and 2017. In 2013, Albert Douer, an experienced executive in [[Building material|construction materials]] and packaging manufacturing, joined the company as a senior strategic investor{{Cite web|url=https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/231415-03#patents|title = UBQ Company Profile: Valuation & Investors | PitchBook}} later becoming chairman of the board and CEO. In 2024, the company opened a full-scale production facility in [[Bergen op Zoom|Bergen op Zoom, the Netherlands]].{{Cite web |date=2024-06-14 |title=UBQ opens industrial-scale production site in the Netherlands |url=https://www.plasticsnews.com/news/ubq-opens-industrial-scale-production-site-netherlands |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Plastics News |language=en}} The plant can process more than 104,600 tonnes of municipal solid waste annually, converting it into up to 80,000 tonnes of UBQ. The Israel facility is now being used as a [[Research and development|Research & Development]] facility. === Funding === Founded in 2012, UBQ Materials raised an initial $3.5 million in [[Seed money|seed funding]] from private investors. In 2013, Albert Douer joined as a senior strategic investor. Between 2013 and 2019, the company secured another $39 million from [[Battery Ventures]], Albert Douer and other private investors. By 2019, its total disclosed funding had reached approximately $42.5 million. In December 2021, UBQ Materials raised $170 million in funding led by TPG Rise Climate and The Rise Funds, TPG’s impact investing platform. The round also featured participation from Battery Ventures and M&G’s Catalyst strategy. As part of the deal, Steve Ellis from The Rise Funds and Ignacio Giraldo from TPG Rise joined UBQ’s board of directors, bringing strategic expertise to scale the business. The investment aligned with TPG Rise’s focus on sustainable technologies with significant environmental benefits. [[J. P. Morgan|J.P. Morgan]] acted as placement agent, and [[Latham & Watkins]] advised UBQ Materials on legal matters for the round. In September 2023, UBQ Materials closed a $70 million financing round led by Eden Global Partners.{{Cite news |date=2023-09-13 |title=UBQ Materials raises $70 million in private funding round |url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/ubq-materials-raises-70-million-private-funding-round-2023-09-13/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |work=Reuters |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Santos |first=Beatriz |date=2024-01-23 |title=UBQ launches sustainable materials, additives portfolio |url=https://www.sustainableplastics.com/news/ubq-launches-sustainable-materials-additives-portfolio |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Sustainable Plastics |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Laird |first=Karen |date=2023-09-13 |title=UBQ closes $70 million funding round |url=https://www.sustainableplastics.com/news/ubq-closes-70-million-funding-round |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Sustainable Plastics |language=en}} The round included returning participants: TPG Rise Climate, TPG’s Rise Fund, Battery Ventures, and M&G’s Catalyst strategy. Eden’s CEO, David Dwek, praised UBQ as a “pioneer” in sustainability and joined the UBQ’s Board of Directors as part of the investment. Over time, UBQ Materials secured an additional $37.5 million in internal funding rounds along with two non-dilutive grants: a US$1.7M grant from the [[Israel Innovation Authority]] (formerly known as Israel Chief Scientist) and a non-dilutive €5 million grant from the EU’s [[Just transition|Just Transition]] Fund in late September 2024.{{Cite web |last=Santos |first=Beatriz |date=2024-09-30 |title=UBQ Materials to receive €5M in EU funds |url=https://www.sustainableplastics.com/news/ubq-materials-receive-eu5m-eu-funds |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Sustainable Plastics |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Dinkovski |first=Noli |date=2024-10-01 |title=UBQ Materials secures €5m Just Transition Fund grant |url=https://ecoplasticsinpackaging.com/bioplastics-biopolymers/ubq-materials-secures-e5m-just-transition-fund-grant/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Eco-plastics in Packaging |language=en-US}} ==Technology== [[Municipal solid waste|Household waste]] is received at the plant in the form of solid residual material (SRM). The mixture runs through stages of automatic refinement, removing particles of metals and minerals that are sent to recycling facilities.{{Cite web|last=Kosciulek|first=Samara Abramson, Mark Abadi, Amelia|title=Investors are pouring billions into the alternative plastics industry — and these companies are racing to deliver|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/plastic-ocean-recycling-investors-sustainable-2020-1|access-date=2020-08-20|website=Business Insider}} The organic waste, like food leftovers, dirty paper and cardboard, is used in its entirety and broken into its basic building blocks, including fibers, [[cellulose]], [[lignin]], [[Collagen|collagens]], and sugars. Conventional plastics are then bound to this matrix, reconstructing them into a new bio-based thermoplastic composite, UBQ. The resulting material is a patented, homogeneous composite, available in tablet or masterbatch form. It can be used with conventional manufacturing equipment for [[Injection moulding|injection molding]], [[extrusion]], [[compression molding]], 3D printing, and [[Rotational molding|rotomolding]] to produce products typically made with oil-based plastics with a reduced [[environmental footprint]].{{Cite web |date=2023-07-13 |title=UBQ Materials wins Plug and Play Sustainability Award |url=https://www.jpost.com/business-and-innovation/all-news/article-750007 |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |language=en |issn=0792-822X }} UBQ thermoplastic is a highly recyclable material contributing to a [[circular economy]]. === Product Portfolio === In January 2024, UBQ Materials launched its diversified product portfolio.{{Cite web |date=2024-01-24 |title=UBQ Materials debuts bio-based solutions for sustainable manufacturing |url=https://www.jpost.com/environment-and-climate-change/article-783491 |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |language=en |issn=0792-822X }} Since then, it has streamlined the offer to focus on high-performing products that align with customers’ needs. UBQ Materials Product Offering: * In May 2025, UBQ Materials introduced the UBQ Masterbatch product line, designed to simplify integration, optimize performance, and scale sustainability across a wide range of applications.{{Cite web |last=Tao |first=Mai |date=2025-05-30 |title=UBQ Materials launches new 'sustainable' plastics range made from household waste |url=https://roboticsandautomationnews.com/2025/05/30/ubq-materials-launches-new-sustainable-plastics-range-made-from-household-waste/91328/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Robotics & Automation News |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |title=Biobased additives, modifiers and material replacements expand UBQ Materials portfolio |url=https://packagingeurope.com/news/biobased-additives-modifiers-and-material-replacements-expand-ubq-materials-portfolio/10908.article |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Packaging Europe |language=en}} * UBQ ClimaPos, a bio-based, climate-positive sustainability additive that enables greenhouse gas removal and avoidance and assists companies in achieving or surpassing ambitious climate objectives. * UBQ Industrial, a material replacement for common plastics, engineered for high impact, durability and reliability in operational uses, while also achieving carbon reduction. * UBQ Nclozur, a sustainability modifier formulated for odor mitigation. UBQ Nclozur is sold only as a modifier to UBQ Materials’ primary additives and replacements. Not sold separately. * UBQ Q Series, a one-to-one material swap that blends with most [[Polymer|polymers]]. This product was discontinued in May 2025. * UBQ Impact, was sold as an enhancer to UBQ Material’s primary additives and material replacements. This product was discontinued in May 2025. ===Application=== UBQ is utilized as a sustainability additive in retail products, furniture,{{Cite web|last=Spiro|first=James|date=2021-04-19|title=Keter Group and UBQ Materials partner to bring sustainable garden goods|url=https://www.calcalistech.com/ctech/articles/0,7340,L-3905332,00.html|access-date=2021-12-15|website=CTECH - www.calcalistech.com}} and within the material supply chain.{{Cite press release|last=Ltd|first=UBQ Materials|title=Bazan Group Inks Deal with UBQ Materials to Incorporate Climate Positive Thermoplastic into Resin Product Lines|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/bazan-group-inks-deal-with-ubq-materials-to-incorporate-climate-positive-thermoplastic-into-resin-product-lines-301407385.html|access-date=2021-12-15|website=www.prnewswire.com|language=en}}UBQ thermoplastic is compatible with existing processes, polymers, and equipment. It works with several standard manufacturing processes and technologies, such as [[Injection moulding|injection molding]], extrusion, compression molding, 3D printing, and rotomolding. UBQ ClimaPos and UBQ Industrial are compatible with [[Polypropylene|PP]], [[Polyethylene|PE]], [[Polylactic acid|PLA]], and [[Polyvinyl chloride|PVC]], while UBQ Masterbatch is compatible with PP, PS, ABS, polyolefins and elastomers. '''Awards''' * UBQ Materials received the [[Zero waste|Zero Waste]] Award, 2021 * UBQ won a SEAL Business Sustainability Award, 2021{{Cite web |last=Laird |first=Karen |date=2021-12-22 |title=UBQ wins a 2021 SEAL Business Sustainability Award |url=https://www.sustainableplastics.com/news/ubq-wins-2021-seal-business-sustainability-award |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Sustainable Plastics |language=en}} * UBQ won the SustainIL Startup Competition, 2021{{Cite web |last=Spiro |first=James |date=2021-01-28 |title=Israel's UBQ Materials and Clairion declared winners of SustainIL Startup Competition |url=https://www.calcalistech.com/ctech/articles/0,7340,L-3890033,00.html |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=CTECH - www.calcalistech.com}} * UBQ Materials and Mercedes-Benz won the [[Decarbonisation|Automotive Sustainability]] Award, 2021{{Cite web |last=Laird |first=Karen |date=2021-05-06 |title=Mercedes-Benz, UBQ Materials recipients Automotive Sustainability award |url=https://www.sustainableplastics.com/news/mercedes-benz-ubq-materials-recipients-automotive-sustainability-award |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Sustainable Plastics |language=en}} * UBQ Materials won the SXSW Innovation Awards, Speculative Design Category, 2022{{Cite web |last=Everett |first=Hayley |date=2022-03-21 |title=UBQ Materials wins 2022 SXSW award for waste-based 3D printing filament |url=https://3dprintingindustry.com/news/ubq-materials-wins-2022-sxsw-award-for-waste-based-3d-printing-filament-206464/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=3D Printing Industry |language=en-US}} * UBQ Materials and Maxion won the Plug and Play Sustainability Award, 2023{{Cite web |title=Maxion en UBQ Materials winnen Plug and Play Sustainability Award op STARTUP AUTOBAHN EXPO2023 |url=https://www.winmagpro.nl/maxion-en-ubq-materials-winnen-plug-and-play-sustainability-award-op-startup-autobahn-expo2023 |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=WINMAG Pro |language=nl}}{{Cite web |date=2023-07-13 |title=UBQ Materials wins Plug and Play Sustainability Award |url=https://www.jpost.com/business-and-innovation/all-news/article-750007 |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |language=en |issn=0792-822X }} * UBQ Materials was named to Time’s List of Best Inventions of 2023, 2023 * UBQ Materials, ConMet, and Polyram won the Supplier Partnership Award, 2023 * UBQ ClimaPos won the Silver Edison Award, 2025 ==Environmental impact== The conversion process uses a closed-loop, energy-efficient process that does not require additional water. It generates no waste effluents, or toxic fumes that could harm human health, air quality, or the climate. UBQ Material’s plant in the Netherlands is highly energy efficient, fully operating on [[Low-carbon electricity|green electricity]] generated by solar or wind power, as certified by [[Guarantee of origin|Guarantees of Origin (GOO)]] generated by solar or wind power.{{Cite news |date=2020-01-22 |title=Daimler to Test UBQ's Climate-positive Material |url=https://www.waste360.com/business-operations/daimler-test-ubqs-climate-positive-material |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606042423/https://www.waste360.com/business-operations/daimler-test-ubqs-climate-positive-material |archive-date=2023-06-06 |access-date=2021-12-15 |work=Waste360 |language=en}} A third-party verified life cycle assessment (LCA) from ERM found that every kilogram of UBQ tablets produced in Bergen op Zoom, the Netherlands, diverts 1.5 kilograms of waste from landfills and incinerators, significantly reducing [[greenhouse gas emissions]] and contributing to a circular economy. A third-party verified [[Life-cycle assessment|life cycle assessment]] (LCA) from ERM found that each kilogram of UBQ tablets removes 1.17 kilograms of CO2eq of biogenic carbon (with cradle to gate boundaries) due to the conversion of organic waste into UBQ, with a production [[carbon footprint]] of only 0.15 kilograms CO2eq per kilogram UBQ tablets. This results in a net cradle-to-gate carbon footprint of -1.02 kilograms CO2eq per kilogram UBQ tablets. UBQ is a [[USDA-certified organic|USDA certified]] bio-preferred material, contains recycled materials, and is [[Recycling|recyclable]] at the end of life.{{Cite web|last=Barrett|first=Axel|date=2021-08-09|title=Origin Materials Gets USDA Certified Biobased Product Label|url=https://bioplasticsnews.com/2021/08/09/origin-materials-usda-certified-biobased-product-label/|access-date=2021-12-15|website=Bioplastics News|language=en-US}} == 2023 Hamas-Israel war == UBQ Materials was among the many Israeli companies affected by the Hamas attack on{{Cite web |date=2023-12-05 |title=Keter company joins forces with startup UBQ located in southern Israel |url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-776717 |access-date=2023-12-06 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |language=en-US |issn=0792-822X}} October 7, 2023. Two employees, Hadar Berdichevsky, former assistant controller and Uri Russo, maintenance and engineering manager, were murdered in their homes.{{Cite web |title=דווקא עכשיו: הסטארטאפים מעוטף עזה מציגים את הפיתוחים שלהם בועידה בדובאי |date=3 December 2023 |url=https://www.geektime.co.il/cop28-dubai-israeli-startups/}}To protect the safety of its staff, UBQ Materials shut down operations at its plant in [[Kibbutz]] [[Tze'elim]] for three weeks. Production resumed on October 30, 2023 and remains fully operational. ==See also== *[[Science and technology in Israel]] ==References== {{reflist}} [[Category:Companies based in Tel Aviv]] [[Category:Israeli companies established in 2012]] [[Category:Recycling companies of Israel]] [[Category:2012 establishments in Israel]] [[Category:Plastic recycling]]

UBQ Materials is a global manufacturing company created to convert mixed household waste including all organic content into a thermoplastic composite. The company's primary product, UBQ, is a bio-based thermoplastic sold in the form of tablets or masterbatch that can replace or enhance conventional plastics in the manufacturing of durable or semi-durable products. UBQ is used in several applications across many industries, specifically in building & construction, consumer durables, supply chain & logistics, automotive, and retail. In 2018, UBQ Materials Ltd. became a Certified B Corporation.
In 2023, Time magazine listed UBQ technology as life-changing.
